output.methodChoice: Combination of C and D: competing explanations tested against where/when contrasts (shift, supplier, time).
output.brief: The jump in chilled write-offs is mainly an internal problem, not a Haverlow problem. Since the night receiving team was cut from six to four in week 31, night pallets take about 3 h 50 min from unload to chamber, up from 44 min. They wait on an unrefrigerated dock at 15–17°C. Night write-off rates rose from 0.6% to 2.9% for every supplier, while day shifts stayed flat. Haverlow's trailer telemetry shows 2–3.5°C at door-open, and trailers were emptied by about 23:00–23:45. The warm "receipt" probes were keyed around 02:30–03:20, after the long wait. So the receiving probe readings reflect dock warming, not supplier abuse. The chambers are fine. Do not raise the chargeback or move Haverlow volume, since that would penalise the wrong party. Do not drop night probing. Lead with restoring night staffing, plus a maximum dock-to-chamber time monitored weekly from scan data. Also sample Corriebank's claims against lots and receiving shift. The 3 August self-certification change plausibly adds some credits, but that is unproven, and part of the credit rise may be real spoilage. Confidence is high on the main cause and moderate on the credits.
